about: Where each measure (MEASURES in server/lib/series-dimensions.js) sits in each structure (server/seed/data/structures/). A placement is { category, basis, tables | reason }: basis 'table' when the structure's publisher puts the measure's data there (the Abstract's table numbers), 'judgement' when GovGraph chose (a sentence saying why). { left_out: true, reason } keeps a measure out of a structure on purpose. All start as judgement (2026-10-13): the Abstract's tables are not read yet (features/statistical-abstract, Phase 2), and CAP sorts policy documents, not statistics. Checked by server/lib/placements.test.js; see features/category-breakdowns.

crude-oil-price.reason: Crude oil prices are the subject of the Crude oil subsection; tables not yet read.

fuel-price.reason: What households pay for fuel, with the other energy prices and expenditures; Prices (Sec. 14) is the alternative.

oil-demand.reason: Product supplied is EIA's measure of petroleum consumption.

unemployment.reason: The Unemployment subsection; tables not yet read.

consumer-prices.reason: The CPI is this subsection's subject; the PCE price index sits with it as the other consumer price measure.

consumer-spending.reason: BEA's personal consumption expenditures are the largest part of GDP, published in the same national accounts; Personal income is the alternative.

consumer-sentiment.reason: The University of Michigan's index is not government data; placed with the other economic indicators.

mortgage-rate.reason: An interest rate, with the other market rates; Home sales (Sec. 20) is the alternative.

home-affordability.reason: Affordability of buying a home, beside home prices.

homeownership.reason: The Homeownership subsection; tables not yet read.

household-income.reason: Census median household income is money income.

interest-rate.reason: The federal funds rate, Treasury yields and the prime rate are market interest rates.

deaths.reason: The Deaths subsection; tables not yet read.

gdp.reason: The Gross domestic product subsection; tables not yet read.

federal-debt.reason: Federal debt is in this subsection's name; tables not yet read.

federal-revenue.reason: Budget receipts; tables not yet read.

tax-credit-payments.reason: Paid out through the Treasury; no Abstract table holds them. Placed with income taxes because they are tax credits.

federal-spending.reason: Budget outlays; tables not yet read.

federal-budget-balance.reason: The surplus or deficit is receipts less outlays, printed beside them.

tax-rate.reason: Income tax rates; tables not yet read.

tax-share.reason: Who pays federal taxes, beside the rates.

top-bracket-threshold.reason: Part of the income tax rate schedule.

tariff-rate.reason: Duties as a share of imports, with the imports they are charged on.

exports.reason: The Exports and imports subsection; tables not yet read.

imports.reason: The Exports and imports subsection; tables not yet read.

trade-balance.reason: Exports less imports, printed beside them; International transactions is the alternative.

fuel-price.reason: Natural Gas & Oil: gasoline and diesel are oil products.

consumer-prices.reason: CAP's Interest Rates subtopic covers inflation, cost of living and prices.

mortgage-rate.reason: Interest Rates; Housing (14) is the alternative.

home-prices.reason: Housing, General: no subtopic for the housing market.

household-income.reason: No subtopic for household income; Macroeconomics, General. A weak fit.

interest-rate.reason: Monetary Policy: the Fed's rate and target range; Interest Rates (101) is the alternative.

deaths.reason: Health, General; Disease Prevention (331) for COVID-19 deaths is the alternative.

federal-revenue.reason: National Budget; Tax Code (107) is the alternative.

tax-share.reason: Tax Code: the impact of taxes.
